title: Reading Compiler Output: if, Loops and switch
summary: Control flow in C++ compiles into a small set of recognisable shapes built from comparisons and jumps. This lesson teaches you to recognise them: `if` and `if`/`else`, `while` and `for` loops (and how compilers rotate them), short-circuit `&&` and `||`, and the **jump table** a `switch` becomes. Recognising shapes is how you read disassembly quickly.
markdown:
## The method When reading compiled code, do not try to understand each instruction in isolation. Look for the **shape**: 1. Find the jumps. Each conditional jump is a decision; each backward jump (to a lower address) is a loop. 2. Group the instructions between jumps into **basic blocks**: straight runs with one way in and one way out. 3. Draw the blocks and the arrows between them. The picture is the control flow, and it maps back to `if`, `while` and `switch`. Disassemblers such as Ghidra and IDA draw this graph for you (chapter 9). With practice you see it directly in the listing. ## if and if/else ```cpp int grade(int score) { if (score >= 50) return 1; return 0; } ``` ```asm cmp ecx, 50 jl fail ; inverted: skip the "then" part when score < 50 mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret ``` With an `else`, the "then" block ends with an unconditional `jmp` over the "else" block to the code after both: ```mermaid flowchart TB A["cmp ...
jcc else"] -->|"condition false"| E["else block"] A -->|"condition true (fall through)"| T["then block
jmp end"] T --> J["end"] E --> J ``` (Optimisers often replace small if/else assignments with `cmov`, lesson 7.04, so there may be no jump at all.) ## Loops A `while` loop literally compiled would test at the top and jump back to the test at the bottom: two jumps per iteration. Compilers **rotate** loops instead: test once before entering, then test again at the bottom with a single backward jump. ```cpp int sum(const int* values, int count) { int total{ 0 }; for (int i{ 0 }; i < count; ++i) total += values[i]; return total; } ``` ```asm xor eax, eax ; total = 0 test edx, edx ; count <= 0? then skip the loop entirely jle done xor r8d, r8d ; i = 0 top: add eax, [rcx+r8*4] ; total += values[i] inc r8d ; ++i cmp r8d, edx ; i < count? jl top ; backward jump: the loop done: ret ``` The **backward jump** to `top` is the signature of a loop. The block before it is the guard that skips the loop when it would run zero times. Step through it with three values: ```demo-asm title: The rotated loop, count = 3 init: rcx=0x2000, edx=3, mem@0x2000=5 7 9 xor eax, eax test edx, edx jle done xor r8d, r8d top: add eax, dword ptr [rcx+r8*4] inc r8d cmp r8d, edx jl top done: ret ``` In optimised builds, loops may also be **unrolled** (the body repeated several times per jump) or **vectorised** (processing four or eight elements per instruction, lesson 7.11), which changes the shape but not the backward jump. ## && and || C++ guarantees **short-circuit** evaluation: in `a && b`, `b` is not evaluated if `a` is false. That becomes a chain of jumps, each able to skip straight to the outcome: ```cpp if (enemy != nullptr && enemy->health > 0) attack(enemy); ``` ```asm test rcx, rcx ; enemy == nullptr? je skip ; then the whole condition is false cmp dword ptr [rcx+8], 0 ; enemy->health > 0? jle skip call attack skip: ``` Two conditional jumps to the same label is the shape of `&&`. For `||`, the first test jumps to the "true" block instead. ## switch and jump tables A `switch` over a few cases compiles to a chain of comparisons. Over many **dense** cases (values close together), the compiler builds a **jump table**: an array of addresses, one per case, and jumps through it with a single indexed jump. ```cpp const char* stateName(int state) { switch (state) { case 0: return "idle"; case 1: return "walking"; case 2: return "running"; case 3: return "jumping"; case 4: return "falling"; default: return "?"; } } ``` ```asm cmp ecx, 4 ja default_case ; unsigned compare: also catches negative values! movsxd rax, ecx lea rdx, [__ImageBase] mov eax, [rdx+rax*4+table_rva] ; read the case's offset from the table add rax, rdx jmp rax ; jump to that case ``` Three things to recognise: - **One unsigned comparison** (`ja`) checks the range: a negative value, seen as unsigned, is huge, so it also goes to `default`. One check covers both ends. - **An indexed load** from a table, scaled by 4 or 8. - **An indirect jump** (`jmp rax`). Sparse cases (1, 100, 5000) get a chain of comparisons or a binary search instead. ## Common mistakes > [!warning] Reading every jump as an `if` > Backward jumps are loops; a `jmp` at the end of a block is usually the "skip the else" jump. > [!warning] Expecting the loop test at the top > Rotated loops test at the bottom, with a guard before the loop. > [!warning] Missing the range check before a jump table > The `cmp` and `ja` before it tell you the number of cases. ## Check yourself ```quiz ? What is a basic block? - One line of C++ source and its instructions + Straight-line code with one entry at the top and one exit - The code between a function's prologue and epilogue - A block of 64 bytes of machine code > Nothing jumps into the middle or out of the middle of a basic block, which makes blocks the boxes of a control-flow graph. ? How does a compiler implement `a && b`? + With jumps: if `a` is false, skip straight past `b` and the body - By computing both, ANDing the results, then testing once - With a single `and` instruction - By calling a helper function that evaluates both sides > `&&` must not evaluate `b` when `a` is false, so the code jumps over it. ? What three parts make up a jump table's code? - A loop over all cases, a compare for each, and a `call` - A signed compare, a `cmov` and a `ret` - A hash of the value, a search, and a direct jump + A range check, a load from a table, and an indirect jump > The range check is one unsigned compare and jump to the default case, which also catches negative values. ? What is the signature of a loop in disassembly? + A conditional jump backwards - Any `cmp` instruction - A `call` > Looping means going back to code that already ran. ? Why does a rotated loop have a test before the loop as well as at the bottom? - Because the CPU requires two tests + To skip the loop entirely when it should run zero times - To count the iterations > The bottom test decides whether to go round again; the guard handles the zero-iteration case. ? Two conditional jumps lead to the same label just before a `call`. What C++ is this likely to be? - `if (a || b) call();` - A `switch` + `if (a && b) call();` > Either condition failing skips the call. ? Why does a jump table's range check use `ja` instead of `jg`? + Unsigned, it also sends negatives to default - `jg` does not exist - The cases are always unsigned > Negative numbers read as unsigned are larger than any case. ```
ideas:
- In the demonstration, trace by hand what happens with `edx=0`: which instructions run?
- Compile the `stateName` switch with `cl /O2 /FA` and find the table. Then make the cases 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 and see whether the table survives.
- Take any function from your own project, open its disassembly, and draw its basic blocks and arrows on paper.
